questions.stem: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence " It is believed that teachers can exert a profound influence on their students' academic pursuit and personal development. " You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words. You should copy the sentence given in quotes at the beginning of your essay.
questions.analysis:
【参考范文】
It is believed that teachers can exert a profound influence on their students' academic pursuit and personal development. Having spent years in classrooms, I firmly agree that a dedicated teacher shapes not only what we learn but also who we become.

On the one hand, teachers guide our academic growth. My high-school chemistry teacher, Mr. Li, turned a subject I once dreaded into my favourite one. By designing vivid experiments and patiently answering my endless questions, he inspired me to pursue science and eventually major in it at university. On the other hand, teachers mould our character. Through his fairness and honesty, Mr. Li taught me to value integrity over easy shortcuts, a lesson that still steers my decisions today.

In conclusion, a good teacher enlightens the mind and cultivates the heart at the same time. Their influence, though quiet and gradual, reaches far beyond examinations and often lasts a whole lifetime.

transcript.zh: W: 我得说，我太喜欢我们的食堂了！那里真是个很棒的碰面地点！

transcript.zh: M: 是啊，对学生和老师来说确实都是这样。就是食物有点可惜。

transcript.text: W: What do you mean? I think the food is fine.
transcript.zh: W: 你这是什么意思？我觉得食物还不错啊。

transcript.text: M: Yeah, those are good. They also come out really fast. Actually, that's one of the best things about the canteen — the speed. If I fancy something more substantial than a sandwich, but I don't have much time for lunch, the university canteen is always a good option. The kitchen staff work at such a brisk pace. They really deserve to be complimented for it.

transcript.zh: W: 完全同意，而且那里的环境也特别好。整个建筑都很漂亮。

transcript.text: M: It is very nice.
transcript.zh: M: 确实很不错。

transcript.zh: W: 那些巨大的玻璃窗让整个地方完全不一样。我觉得它们特别酷。听说他们几年前进行了一次大规模翻修，花了不少钱。

transcript.text: M: Yeah, I'm not surprised. It's a very versatile space, suitable both for eating and relaxing.
transcript.zh: M: 是啊，我一点也不意外。那是个用途非常灵活的空间，既适合吃饭，也适合放松。

questions.stem: What does the woman say about the food at the canteen?

options.text: It brings shame on the university.
It caters to students and teachers.

questions.analysis: 态度观点题。答案句（P5）：W: I don't, actually. I personally think they're perfectly appropriate.信号：被问者的直接应答 + 转折否定 。男士先抛出 the prices are absurd 并反问 Don't you agree，女士的应答 I don't, actually 是一句明确的否定回应，紧接 I per…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：It is absurdly expensive. 直接挪用了录音里的 absurd，但说 the prices are absurd 的是男士、不是女士，女士恰恰否定了这一点。听到 absurd 就选 A，正中『听到原词就选』的陷阱。 借用原文：Shame about the food.
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：It brings shame on the university. 借用了录音里的 shame，但男士那句 Shame about the food. 是英式口语『可惜了这食物』的意思，并非『给学校丢脸』，且也不是女士对食物的评价。听到 shame 就联想到『丢脸』属于偷换概念。 借用原文：both for students and teachers
optionAnalysis.D: 答非所问：It caters to students and teachers. 挪用了录音 both for students and teachers，但那是男士在说食堂作为聚会点适合师生，谈的是场所、不是『食物』，与题目问的食物评价不沾边。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（perfectly appropriate ↔ appropriately priced 同根词改写：appropriate→appropriately priced）

They are never actually good value.

questions.analysis: 态度观点题。答案句（P7）：I never really crave sweet things or any fancy delicacies.信号：含蓄否定 never...crave 表态度 。女士说 I never really crave sweet things or any fancy delicacies，crave（渴望）配 never 是一句明确…

optionAnalysis.B: 答非所问：They are never actually good value. 蹭了录音里关于价格的讨论（desserts are overpriced），但题目问的是女士对甜点的『感受/兴趣』，女士给出的态度是『不想吃』，而非评价它们『不划算』。把态度偷换成性价比。 借用原文：beyond most students' budgets
optionAnalysis.C: 与原文相反：They are within students' budgets. 挪用了前文男士谈预算的 beyond most students' budgets，且与原文相反（男士说甜点超出预算），更何况它讲的是价格不是女士的态度，双重错位。 借用原文：They also come out really fast
optionAnalysis.D: 张冠李戴：They always come at a high speed. 借用了录音里关于上菜快的描述（They also come out really fast），但那是男士夸炒蛋出餐快，被安到了甜点和女士态度上，张冠李戴又答非所问。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（I never really crave sweet things or any fancy delicacies ↔ They never really appeal to her. 主被动视角转换：我不想要它→它不吸引我）

optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（the speed ↔ The speed. 原词直接对应）

questions.stem: What did the canteen undergo a few years ago?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P11）：Apparently, they did a massive renovation a few years ago.信号：时间状语 a few years ago 标记答案句 。女士说 they did a massive renovation a few years ago，时间状语 a few years ago 与题干完全对上，是…

optionAnalysis.A: 偷换概念：A complete refurnishing. 蹭了改造话题，但 refurnishing 是『重新配置家具』，与录音 a massive renovation（整体翻新）程度和性质都不同，是偷换概念。 借用原文：a massive renovation
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：A ruinous burning down. 是『毁灭性烧毁』，录音通篇在夸食堂漂亮、做过翻新，根本没提任何火灾，纯属无中生有。
optionAnalysis.C: 偷换概念：A substantial expansion. 与答案 D 同样表『大规模』，借 massive/substantial 的近似制造混淆，但 expansion 是『扩建、变大』，录音说的是 renovation（翻新），并非扩大面积，差在动作名词上。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（a massive renovation ↔ A massive renovation. 原词对应，但需与近义项 expansion 切开）

transcript.text: W: Hi, Tony, today we're talking about how managers can get along better with young people at work. We often hear young people today have a poor work ethic. That's not really justified though, is it?
transcript.zh: W: 嗨，托尼，今天我们来谈谈管理者如何在工作中更好地与年轻人相处。我们经常听到有人说，如今的年轻人职业道德较差。不过，这种说法其实并没有什么依据，对吧？

transcript.text: M: Not really. In reality, young people of this age group are as varied and multifaceted as any other generation.
transcript.zh: M: 确实没有。实际上，这个年龄段的年轻人和其他任何一代人一样，都是多种多样、各具特点的。

transcript.text: W: Yeah, but if you are struggling to work with young people in your workspace, what can you do?
transcript.zh: W: 是的，但如果你在工作中和年轻人合作时遇到了困难，你能做些什么呢？

transcript.text: M: Well, it's essential to connect with them to learn about their values. It's also really important to recognize the way young people want to balance their work life with their personal life.
transcript.zh: M: 首先，必须与他们建立联系，了解他们的价值观。同样重要的是，要认识到年轻人希望如何平衡工作与个人生活。

transcript.text: W: So they generally don't want to defer happiness in return for career advancement?
transcript.zh: W: 所以，他们通常不想为了事业发展而推迟享受生活？

transcript.text: M: Absolutely. They are not willing to sacrifice their personal lives for their work lives and this leads people to equate that with an unwillingness to work hard.
transcript.zh: M: 完全正确。他们不愿意为了工作生活而牺牲个人生活，而这就导致人们把这种态度等同于不愿意努力工作。

transcript.text: W: Right. But that couldn't be further from the truth, could it?
transcript.zh: W: 没错。但事实完全不是这样，对吧？

transcript.text: M: Young people will work extremely hard during their defined work hours, but they expect to have their time off, like weekends and nights free from work.
transcript.zh: M: 年轻人在规定的工作时间内会非常努力地工作，但他们希望自己的休息时间，比如周末和晚上，不受工作打扰。

transcript.text: W: So how should managers go about assessing young people's productivity?
transcript.zh: W: 那么，管理者应该如何评估年轻人的工作效率呢？

transcript.text: M: Generally, young people believe their productivity should not be measured by the number of hours they work, since someone can work for eight hours and accomplish next to nothing of significance for the company. Instead, young people measure their productivity levels by the quality of the work they perform.
transcript.zh: M: 总的来说，年轻人认为，工作效率不应该用工作时长来衡量，因为有人可能工作八个小时，却几乎没有为公司完成任何有意义的事情。相反，年轻人会根据自己完成的工作质量来衡量工作效率。

transcript.text: W: But we often hear that young people want to feel more than just being a part of a big machine. Such a perspective can be hard to discredit, can't it?
transcript.zh: W: 但我们经常听到，年轻人希望感受到的不只是自己属于一台庞大机器的一部分。这种观点很难反驳，对吧？

transcript.text: M: It's important to legitimize their work. Young workers want to work on projects that matter to themselves, the company or the world at large. They must feel the need to stay working at a company whose values align with their own.
transcript.zh: M: 认可他们工作的价值很重要。年轻人希望参与对自己、公司或整个世界都有意义的项目。他们必须觉得，公司所秉持的价值观与自己的价值观一致，这样才愿意继续在那里工作。

transcript.text: W: Thanks for your advice.
transcript.zh: W: 谢谢你的建议。

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：We often hear young people today have a poor work ethic. That's not really justified though, is it?信号：女方自问句 + that's not justified 。答案句出自女方之口：先抛出常见说法 young people today have a poor work ethic，紧接 That's not real…

optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：选项 They don't get along with managers. 盗用了对话主题里反复出现的 managers，但女方在 P1 里判为「站不住脚」的说法是职业道德差，从没说年轻人和管理者合不来，属答非所问。 借用原文：if you are struggling to work with young people
optionAnalysis.C: 张冠李戴：选项 They are struggling in the workplace. 借了后文 if you are struggling to work with young people 里的 struggling，但那是说「管理者难以与年轻人共事」，并非女方在第 1 段判为不成立的看法，张冠李戴。 借用原文：as varied and multifaceted as any other generation
optionAnalysis.D: 张冠李戴：选项 They aren't as varied as their predecessors. 与男方 young people of this age group are as varied and multifaceted as any other generation 正好相反：男方说「和任何一代一样多样」，选项却说「不如前人多样」，极性被反转，且这话也不是女方所说。

options.text: Learning about the way they adhere to their own values.

options.text: In terms of the number of hours spent.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P10）：Generally, young people believe their productivity should not be measured by the number of hours they work, since someone can work for eight hours and accomplish next to nothing of significance for the company. transcript.text: 1 Many restaurants are trying to persuade customers to eat more sustainably, moving away from environmentally unfriendly meat towards greener dishes.

Although it sounds counter-intuitive, restaurants which include specific vegetarian sections on their menus may be unintentionally encouraging customers to eat meat, a new study suggests. 2 Behavioral scientist Linda Bacon, one of the study's authors, said, "Restaurants can have a positive impact on the environment by encouraging their customers to choose more plant-based food and less meat.

However, our findings suggest that while certain restaurant menu designs can encourage some consumers to make pro-environmental food choices, they can have the opposite effect on others." The study involved 750 people, half of whom frequently ate vegetarian food and half of whom rarely ate it.
No vegetarians were included.
They were given different menus and asked to choose a meal as if they were eating out with friends.
Placing vegetarian dishes in a separate section did not have a significant effect on the choices made by infrequent vegetarian food eaters.
But it did have a notable effect on the frequent eaters, lowering their chance of picking a vegetarian option by 65%.

The researchers also discovered that presenting a vegetarian dish as the chef's recommendation, or including a more appealing description of a non-meat meal, leads to a greater proportion of infrequent vegetarian eaters choosing a vegetarian option.
But again, these altered menu designs backfired with those who ate vegetarian food more frequently, leading them to be less likely to choose a vegetarian dish.

They found that if pollution is frozen to around –18 ℃ in a condensing tube, the particles gather together and fall to the bottom, allowing fresh, clean air to pass through.
Their method was able to remove 99% of pollutants.

When outdoor air quality is poor, people tend to spend even more time indoors.
But outdoor pollution also leads to indoor pollution, and people still suffer.
It is estimated that pollution is linked to over 40,000 early deaths in Britain each year.

Professor Gang Pan of the Chinese Academy of Sciences said, "We have shown in our experiments that simply by circulating polluted air through a small freezing chamber, we can remove most of the fine particles and gas pollutants.
Our study makes it possible to add an air cleaner option to household appliances in areas which might experience extremely poor air conditions.

transcript.text: Research recently carried out by my team suggests that fish may be self-aware. A certain species of fish recently passed the well-known mirror test.
transcript.zh: 我的团队最近开展的研究表明，鱼类可能具有自我意识。最近，有一种鱼通过了著名的镜子测试。

transcript.text: This is a test that demonstrates self-recognition in animals. Only a few animals, such as humans, apes, dolphins and some birds, can recognize themselves in a mirror. And only these animals, capable of self-recognition, will attempt to remove marks placed on their skin after noticing them in the reflection. This ability suggests a level of higher intelligence and awareness. This is not shown by children until around 18 months. Until now, no fish has demonstrated the ability. But our experiments show the fish in question will scrape up against hard surfaces to remove marks placed on its body by our researchers after viewing itself in a mirror. The behaviors we observe leave little doubt that this fish behaviorally fulfills all criteria of the mirror test as originally laid out. The fish in our study never attempted to remove the marks when no mirror was present or when the marks were just placed on the mirror. Unmarked fish also did not attempt to remove marks from themselves when interacting with a marked fish on the other side of a window. These results show either that fish are self-aware or that the mirror test, which is considered to be the gold standard test used to denote higher intelligence, may be flawed.
transcript.zh: 这是一项用来证明动物具有自我识别能力的测试。只有少数动物，例如人类、猿类、海豚和一些鸟类，能够在镜子中认出自己。也只有这些具有自我识别能力的动物，才会在倒影中注意到皮肤上的标记后，试图将其去除。这种能力表明动物具有较高程度的智力和意识。儿童要到大约18个月大时才会表现出这种能力。到目前为止，还没有鱼类展示过这种能力。但我们的实验表明，这种鱼在镜子中看到自己后，会在坚硬的表面上摩擦身体，以去除研究人员放在它身上的标记。我们观察到的行为几乎毫无疑问地表明，这种鱼在行为上满足了镜子测试最初设定的全部标准。我们的研究中的鱼在没有镜子时，或标记只是被放在镜子上时，从未试图去除这些标记。未被标记的鱼在隔着窗户与另一侧的被标记鱼互动时，也没有试图去除自己身上的标记。这些结果表明，要么鱼类具有自我意识，要么被视为判定较高智力的黄金标准测试的镜子测试存在缺陷。

transcript.text: What is less clear is whether these behaviors should be considered as evidence that fish are self-aware, even though in the past these same behaviors have been interpreted as self-awareness in so many other animals. Depending on your position, you might reject the interpretation that these behaviors in a fish satisfy passing the test at all. But on what objective basis can you do this when the behaviors they show are so functionally similar to those of other species that have passed the test?
transcript.zh: 不太明确的是，尽管过去人们一直将其他许多动物的这些相同行为解释为自我意识的表现，但这些行为是否应被视为鱼类具有自我意识的证据。根据你的立场，你可能完全拒绝接受这样的解释，即鱼类的这些行为足以满足通过该测试的条件。但是，当鱼类表现出的行为在功能上与其他通过测试的物种如此相似时，你又能以什么客观依据这样做呢？

transcript.text: Results from our research raise more questions than answers. What if self-awareness develops like an onion, building layer upon layer rather than appearing all at once? Perhaps in order to explore self-awareness further, we should stop looking at responses to the mirror as a decisive test. Only with a richer theory of the self and a larger test battery will we be able to determine all of the various levels of self-awareness, including where exactly fish fit in.
transcript.zh: 我们的研究结果提出的问题多于给出的答案。如果自我意识像洋葱一样逐层发展，而不是一下子全部出现，会怎么样？也许，为了进一步探究自我意识，我们应该不再把对镜子的反应视为决定性测试。只有建立起更丰富的自我理论，并采用规模更大的测试组合，我们才能确定自我意识的各种不同层次，包括鱼类究竟处于其中的哪个位置。

transcript.text: Reading with a young child is important. But does it matter whether you read from an electronic book or traditional print? As any parent knows, small children are generally keen on screens. So the finding from a new study that very young children enjoy electronic books more than printed picture books may not come as a huge surprise — but the following additional findings might: both parents and children behaved differently when reading electronic versus printed picture books. And the children who read the electronic books learned more.
transcript.zh: 与年幼的孩子一起阅读很重要。但从电子书还是传统纸质书阅读，这一点是否有区别呢？正如任何家长都知道的那样，幼儿通常都很喜欢屏幕。因此，一项新研究发现，幼儿更喜欢电子书而不是纸质图画书，这或许并不令人十分意外——但接下来的附加发现可能会让人感到意外：家长和孩子在阅读电子图画书与纸质图画书时的行为有所不同。而且，阅读电子书的孩子学到了更多内容。

transcript.text: Previous studies of young children have suggested that electronic books, which incorporate extra features such as dictionaries and images that depict story events, may have advantages over print. In fact, multiple studies have found that electronic books support story comprehension and vocabulary gains beyond what is provided by printed books. But there's also work suggesting that children sometimes invest less mental effort in learning from electronic books, and that parents talk less about content when sharing such books.
transcript.zh: 此前针对幼儿的研究表明，电子书加入了词典、描绘故事情节的图片等额外功能，因此可能比纸质书更具优势。事实上，多项研究发现，电子书在促进故事理解和词汇增长方面，所起的作用超出了纸质书所能提供的效果。但也有研究表明，孩子有时在从电子书中学习时投入的脑力较少，而且家长与孩子共同阅读电子书时，对内容谈论得也比较少。

transcript.text: The study we're looking at today aims to give us a better understanding of how good electronic books are for young children. For this study, researchers videoed children aged 17 to 26 months reading with one of their parents. Each parent-child pair was randomly assigned to read either two educational electronic books or two printed books with the same content. While the parent read the words in the printed books aloud, the electronic books had audio of voice actors reading the text.
transcript.zh: 我们今天要了解的这项研究，旨在帮助我们更好地理解电子书对幼儿究竟有多大益处。在这项研究中，研究人员拍摄了17至26个月大的孩子与其中一位家长共同阅读的过程。每一对家长和孩子被随机分配阅读两本教育类电子书，或两本内容相同的纸质书。家长大声朗读纸质书中的文字，而电子书则配有配音演员朗读文本的音频。

transcript.text: The researchers found that parents who read the printed books pointed more frequently to pages than parents who read the electronic books. But the opposite was true for the children. Children who read the electronic books also commented more on the content and learned more new words than the children who read printed books.
transcript.zh: 研究人员发现，阅读纸质书的家长比阅读电子书的家长更频繁地指向书页。但孩子的情况正好相反。阅读电子书的孩子还会更多地评论书中内容，并且比阅读纸质书的孩子学会更多新词。

transcript.text: This greater learning is ascribed to greater engagement with the electronic books. It's important to note that the electronic books in the study were simple. While they included background music, animation and sound effects, there were no other extra features.
transcript.zh: 这种更好的学习效果被归因于孩子对电子书更高的参与度。需要注意的是，这项研究中的电子书很简单。虽然其中包含背景音乐、动画和音效，但没有其他额外功能。

transcript.text: It's also important to note that there's research on older children, finding that electronic books don't always bolster learning. Parents and educators need to beware. Extra features in electronic books may increase children's participation with them; however, if these features don't draw attention to the educational content, they may not serve as a supportive feature.
transcript.zh: 同样需要注意的是，针对年龄较大儿童的研究发现，电子书并不总能促进学习。家长和教育工作者需要对此保持警惕。电子书中的额外功能可能会提高孩子对电子书的参与度；然而，如果这些功能不能将孩子的注意力吸引到教育内容上，那么它们可能就无法起到支持作用。

questions.stem: What finding from the new study might come as a huge surprise?

options.text: Small children are even more keen on screens than their elders.
Both parents and children preferred to read electronic books.
Parents differed from children in reading behavior.
Children reading electronic books learned more.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：So the finding from a new study that very young children enjoy electronic books more than printed picture books may not come as a huge surprise — but the following additional findings might: both parents and children behaved differently when reading electronic versus printed picture books. And the children who read the electronic books learned more.信号：转折 but…might 指向真正的意外 。录音先用 may not come as a huge surprise 把"小孩爱电子书"排掉，紧接 but the following additional findi…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：Small children are even more keen on screens than their elders. 借用了录音 small children are generally keen on screens 的原词，但录音说这是"也许并不令人意外"的前提，与题面要的"意外发现"正相反，听到 keen on screens 就选会中招。 借用原文：both parents and children behaved differently
optionAnalysis.B: 偷换概念：Both parents and children preferred to read electronic books. 套用了录音 both parents and children behaved differently 里的 both parents and children，却把 behaved differently（表现不同）偷换成 preferred to read electronic books（都偏爱电子书），原文从没说父母也偏爱电子书。 借用原文：both parents and children behaved differently
optionAnalysis.C: 答非所问：Parents differed from children in reading behavior. 确实对应 both parents and children behaved differently，本身没说错，但题干特别问"令人意外"的发现，录音的 surprise 落点落在"孩子学得更多"上；C 是 but 后并列的发现之一，却不是题面聚焦的那一条，被更贴题的 D 比下去。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（the children who read the electronic books learned more ↔ Children reading electronic books learned more 近乎同义、仅句式微调）

optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：They were based on small samples. 谈以往研究的样本量，但录音讲 previous studies 时只对比了结论方向，全程没说过样本大小，属凭"评价研究常谈样本"的常识硬填。
optionAnalysis.C: 张冠李戴：They yielded unanticipated findings. 里 unanticipated 蹭了第 1 段 huge surprise 的"意外"概念，但那是形容"本次新研究"的发现；本题问的是 previous studies（以往研究），张冠李戴。 借用原文：there's research on older children
optionAnalysis.D: 偷换概念：They were focused on younger kids. 借了录音反复出现的 young children 概念，但录音说的是"也有针对 older children 的研究"，并未限定以往研究都只盯更小的孩子，把研究对象范围说窄了。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（multiple studies have found that electronic books support story comprehension and vocabulary gains ↔ They came to conflicting conclusions 正反两面概括为"矛盾"）

But there's also work suggesting that children sometimes invest less mental effort in learning from electronic books, and that parents talk less about content when sharing such books.

questions.stem: What extra features should be included in electronic books to bolster children's learning?

options.text: Those that prove simple enough for them to comprehend.
Those that produce both audio and visual effects on them.
Those that draw their attention to the educational content.
Those that contribute to their increased interest in reading.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P6）：Extra features in electronic books may increase children's participation with them; however, if these features don't draw attention to the educational content, they may not serve as a supportive feature.信号：however + if 否定句给出条件 。录音先承认 Extra features…may increase children's participation，再用 however, if these featur…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：Those that prove simple enough for them to comprehend. 蹭了第 5 段 the electronic books in the study were simple 的 simple，但那只是描述研究所用电子书的特点，录音从没说"简单到能懂"是促进学习该加的功能，听到 simple 就选会落坑。 借用原文：they included background music, animation and sound effects
optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：Those that produce both audio and visual effects on them. 直接搬录音 they included background music, animation and sound effects 的音乐、动画、音效，这些恰是"声光效果"，但录音的落点是"光有这些额外功能、若不指向教育内容就没用"，B 把被否定的诱饵当成了答案。 借用原文：Extra features in electronic books may increase children's participation with them
optionAnalysis.D: 偷换概念：Those that contribute to their increased interest in reading. 像是改写自录音 Extra features…may increase children's participation，但录音说的是 increase participation（提高参与度），并把它和"促进学习"区分开（参与高未必学得好），选项把它换成 increased interest in reading（提高阅读兴趣）且当成促学习的条件，偷换且跑题。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（if these features don't draw attention to the educational content, they may not serve as a supportive feature ↔ Those that draw their attention to the educational content 否定条件转正面、原词点对）

transcript.text: Let me be honest with you. If you're living your life full of regrets, you're wasting your time. Why would you go through life regretting the very decisions that made you who you are today? There are plenty of unfavorable decisions we've made, but does that mean we should regret them? No!
transcript.zh: 让我坦诚地告诉你。如果你满怀悔恨地生活，就是在浪费时间。你为什么要在一生中不断后悔那些造就了今天的你的决定呢？我们做过许多不利的决定，但这是否意味着我们应该后悔？不！

transcript.text: I've had many moments where I sit and think about all the things I wish I could have done differently. However, just because things could be different, it doesn't necessarily mean they would be better. You don't have to continually be thinking of all your past decisions and whether or not you made the right one. You can't go back and change anything, so what's the point in worrying about it?
transcript.zh: 我曾有过许多时候，坐下来思考所有那些我希望自己能够做得不同的事情。然而，仅仅因为事情本可以有所不同，并不一定意味着结果会更好。你不必一直思考过去所做的每一个决定，以及自己是否做出了正确的选择。你无法回到过去改变任何事情，那么又何必为此担忧呢？

transcript.text: Every single decision you've ever made, positive or negative, has made you the person you are today. We want to go back and change parts of our past, but what would be the benefit of that? We would have lost the valuable knowledge from the lessons we learned.
transcript.zh: 你曾经做出的每一个决定，无论积极还是消极，都造就了今天的你。我们想回到过去，改变过去的一些部分，但那样做会有什么益处呢？我们会失去从所学教训中获得的宝贵知识。

transcript.text: There are reasons you make the choices you do, and that tells us about who you are. So when it comes to any decision in life, be unapologetically yourself. Because at the end of the day, it was you who made that decision.
transcript.zh: 你所做的每个选择都有其原因，而这些原因体现了你是怎样的人。因此，当你面对人生中的任何决定时，都要毫不 apologetically 地做自己。因为归根结底，是你做出了那个决定。

transcript.text: With less time spent focused on regrets, you'll finally have time to focus on the more essential things in life. In any situation, you grow more as a person with every decision you make. Life is full of lessons to learn, so we can't let regret stop us from moving forward.
transcript.zh: 少花些时间专注于悔恨，你终于会有时间去关注生活中更重要的事情。在任何情况下，你都会随着自己做出的每一个决定而不断成长。生活充满了值得学习的教训，所以我们不能让悔恨阻止我们继续前进。

transcript.text: We don't know if we've made the right or wrong choice until after it's already been made, so it can be easy to start regretting your decision. But if the decision has already been made, what's the purpose of dwelling on it? There isn't one. All you can do is move forward. You can't let yourself sit there and worry about every past choice. We aren't all perfect.
transcript.zh: 在一个选择已经做出之前，我们不知道它究竟是正确的还是错误的，所以很容易开始后悔自己的决定。但如果决定已经做出，反复纠结它又有什么意义呢？没有任何意义。你能做的只有继续向前。你不能让自己坐在那里，为过去做出的每一个选择忧虑不已。我们都不可能完美。

transcript.text: Whenever you make a decision, there will always be a possibility for regret later, but that's how life is supposed to be. You will make poor decisions in life — we all do — but it's what you do with the lessons learned that matters.
transcript.zh: 每当你做出一个决定，之后总有可能产生悔恨，但人生本来就应该是这样。你会在人生中做出糟糕的决定——我们都会如此——但真正重要的是，你如何对待从中吸取的教训。

transcript.text: Think about every decision you've ever made. Were they always the best? Of course not. But look at how far you've come since then.
transcript.zh: 想想你曾经做出的每一个决定。它们是否总是最好的？当然不是。但看看从那时起你已经走了多远。

options.text: Regret having wasted much time in making them.

Live with them for the time being.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：If you're living your life full of regrets, you're wasting your time.... There are plenty of unfavorable decisions we've made, but does that mean we should regret them? No!信号：反问加 No 的强烈否定 。does that mean we should regret them? No! 用'反问 + 斩钉截铁的 No'把态度顶到最高：不该后悔。这种自问自答后紧跟否定的句子，正是演讲者亮出主…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：A 把原文里 living your life full of regrets, you're wasting your time 的两个原词 regret 和 wasting time 拼到一起，做成 Regret having wasted much time in making them.，但原文说'后悔本身是浪费时间'，A 却变成'为浪费时间而后悔'，听到原词就选必中招。 借用原文：just because things could be different, it doesn't necessarily mean they would be better

optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：Live with them for the time being. 主张'暂且与这些决定共处'，但原文从头到尾讲的是'别后悔、向前看'，并没有说'暂且忍受'这种过渡性态度，属于无中生有。

passages.title: Section B 长篇阅读匹配

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Projects, relationships, and jobs don't always work out as planned — and it's not always clear when to give up. We've all repeatedly heard the saying that "quitters never win", but sometimes the best decision is to cut our losses.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Think about that relationship you held on to even after it had run its course or the job you stayed in despite your boss making you miserable. Many of us try to hold onto the last ray of hope, thinking we can make it work, whatever "it" is. And while perseverance is generally an excellent quality, it may also incline you to over-invest in something that is no longer a good idea.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: As an executive coach, I work with numerous passionate and hard-working leaders who don't want to "quit". But the smartest leaders learn to discern the difference between quitting too soon and holding onto something that they shouldn't.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: We are all susceptible to the sunk-cost delusion, an unconscious bias that leads us to persist in an endeavor we have already invested time, effort, or money into — even when abandoning it would be more beneficial. We realize that we can't get back the resources we've given, so we persevere — investing in a project that should be halted, staying in a relationship that should be over, or finishing a book we no longer enjoy and should put down, because we're already halfway through it. If quitting is "not your thing", you may be especially susceptible to this bias.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: The sunk-cost delusion causes us to overly worry about what we'll lose if we move on and not think enough about the costs of not moving on. To offset this bias, deliberately refocus your thinking on the gains so you can more objectively weigh the alternatives. Ask yourself: What might I gain by cutting my losses now? Will you be happier or have time for another (better) opportunity? Then ask yourself: What will it cost me to soldier on? For example, is it possible that you'll be throwing more good money after what you've already lost? Or that you won't have the energy to capitalize on other promising possibilities?

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: The illusion of control can also interfere with our best judgment, leading us to overestimate our ability to control events and attain a positive outcome. This bias gives us a sense of agency and can promote mental health. However, the bias can also result in escalating commitment to a losing course of action. Especially when combined with an "I'm not a quitter" mentality, feeling like we have more control over an event or person than we do puts us at risk of doubling down when we should pull out.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: To counteract this bias, consider your situation and make a simple two-column list of what's in your control and what's not. Think rigorously. While you may be able to influence other people and various circumstances, you can't force them to change or go your way.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: Getting clear on what you can control and what you can't is essential to making a quality decision about whether to call it quits or persevere. With a written list in hand, you can ensure you focus on what you can control and better assess whether your continued efforts are worth the expense. Expending effort and emotion on things you can't control can be both draining and disempowering.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: Research indicates that people link their self-identity and social status to their commitments. And because we identify with our commitments, withdrawing from one can feel like a threat to our identity or status.

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: Take my client Ryan, a leader at a technology company. Ryan had invested two years and a lot of effort in a design project that wasn't delivering the needed outcomes, but the thought of abandoning it after all she had put in was hard to bear. As Ryan and I explored whether she should cancel the initiative she'd been leading or continue to persevere, she stated, "The thing is, I'm not a quitter." This singular, fixed sense of self was clouding her judgment and limiting her choices for action.

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: Our self-concept and identity are mental concepts that influence our behavior. If you strongly identify as not being a quitter, you can end up staying stuck in a course of action due to your narrow and rigid self-concept. To overcome this kind of internal obstacle, recall your other positive traits and personality characteristics. Ask yourself: What additional strengths do I have (or aspire to have) that would be helpful to employ here? For example, when I asked Ryan what other positive qualities from her personality she needed to leverage for decision making, she replied, "Discernment and bravery."

paragraphs.label: L
paragraphs.text: Now, examine your situation through the lens of each of these facets of yourself. What does the discerning part of you say? The brave part? Considering your decision through these different characteristics will enable you to see that you have more choices. It's also helpful to seek external sources of information, rather than relying solely on your thinking and instincts. But it's important to think through whose opinions you solicit.

paragraphs.label: M
paragraphs.text: Ideally, seek out people who are less invested in your decision than you are. If you're considering whether to shut down your entrepreneurial venture, for instance, reach out to other founders as opposed to just your business partner. Similarly, if you're looking for love advice, ask someone removed from the ups and downs of your relationship instead of relying only on your best friend. In all cases, I recommend describing your situation and following up with a question like: "How would you manage this situation?"

paragraphs.label: N
paragraphs.text: Alternately, you could also seek out hard data that illuminates your real chance of success in whatever endeavor you are contemplating. Sticking with the example of the entrepreneurial venture, numbers are your best friend. Use them to remove yourself from the love you have for this idea and consider your burn rate relative to growth plan, industry growth rates, and other factors that predict start-up success. External sources of information can help you see angles and possibilities you might not have considered.

paragraphs.label: O
paragraphs.text: When something that seemed so promising at the start doesn't turn out the way we imagined, we can become overly self-critical. Nobody likes to feel that they've made a poor decision, especially if making intelligent decisions is a quality you hold in high esteem. The most effective strategy here is to give yourself a break. Practicing self-compassion increases your resilience(韧性), emotional intelligence, compassion toward others, and can boost your performance as well as help you develop a growth mindset.

paragraphs.label: P
paragraphs.text: Instead of deliberating and criticizing yourself, focus instead on what you can learn from this situation. For example, Ryan recognized she had developed various new skills and leadership capabilities from leading the design project. And despite ultimately deciding to drop it, she was still happy she had tried and grateful for what the experience taught her.

paragraphs.label: Q
paragraphs.text: Undeniably, perseverance can help us succeed. But for your well-being, it's important to learn how to distinguish quitting too soon and clinging to a losing course of action. While letting go can be difficult, it will free up your time, energy, and mental space to imagine new possibilities and pursue new opportunities.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: As interdependent beings we cannot thrive independent of others. We like to work with people who are like-minded, with whom we share a common interest, or who also believe in a cause we are serious about. This is evident in how we have organized ourselves into various collective groups such as nations, regions, communities, organizations, and families.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Does the group you belong to have a strong collective consciousness or shared beliefs? Is there interdependence among its members? Do you consider this group a significant part of your existence? If your answers are affirmative, then you are experiencing a micro version of solidarity.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: What is solidarity? Its simplest definition in the dictionary is: "… a unifying opinion, feeling, purpose or interest among a group of people."

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: In this increasingly diverse society we live in, solidarity takes on a complex and multifaceted character as it forms bonds of interdependence among unique individuals living in a fast-changing environment and working within a complex division of labor.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: One facet of solidarity fits well with the principles of communitarianism(社群主义). In this setting, individuals give up their own interests to serve the common good. However, its strict adherence to social cohesiveness and exclusiveness restricts expression and practice of individual differences and preferences. Consequently, individuality and autonomy are sacrificed to maintain the unity of the group.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Solidarity is also viewed as a reaction to the extreme emphasis on individualism and freedom of choice. It goes against the liberal idea of unrestricted individuals who see society as a hindrance to their freedom to make choices and to act according to what is good for them regardless of how these will affect others.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: But despite its many facets, social theorists have viewed solidarity as a key factor in bringing about order and progress in society. They believe that for human society to survive as it becomes more diverse, more new bonds need to be formed based on the differences. In the light of this, they regard a genuine solidarity as more than just shallow relationships based on common interests. Solidarity is not just a product of strategic calculations of how much it will benefit the self. It is not an exclusive class founded on the you-and-me-against-the-world principle. Rather, it is inclusive and is not forced. Acting out of solidarity means supporting and standing up for each other — in recognition that one's fate is in the fate of the other. It is a bond characterized by cooperative practices and strengthened by the concern for the well-being of others or the common good. It fights for the protection of human dignity and listens to and acts on the cries of the most vulnerable.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: When someone is giving advice in order to make themselves feel more powerful, there is underlying anxiety to their behavior that recipients of the advice tend to notice. It can be tempting in this situation to react harshly to the advice giver and to accuse them of being manipulative, but this approach might produce an undesired result.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: If the act of giving advice is contributing actively to someone's feelings of self-worth, an outright(直率的) rejection may be perceived as a threat, activating their fight-or-flight response, possibly causing them to double down on their validation-seeking behavior, or leading to a larger conflict.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: The key is to validate without over-identifying. You can let them know that you have heard them and appreciate where they are coming from without taking on the potentially damaging narrative that you could not have gotten by without their help. You had better say something like, "Thanks for the idea. I have my own plan for handling this, but I really appreciate your perspective and will take it into consideration. Can I let you know when I need help in the future?"

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: If you have trouble setting boundaries tactfully, prioritize working on your own ability to self-regulate. As uncomfortable as it may be to continuously receive, if you can respond with compassion, the situation will likely defuse much faster.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: Though it is usually not the intended outcome of giving unsolicited advice, many who receive it often feel stressed, offended, or simply annoyed by unwanted suggestions. Setting a boundary in this regard, if you feel you need one, is perfectly reasonable and something that can bring you increased emotional safety.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: It is best to set boundaries in a way that takes into account the individual's underlying reasons for doing what they are doing to avoid unnecessary conflict and more stress.
